title: On-device AI Insights in Fitzenia (vs. the AI Coach)
chunks: AI Insights are short, plain-language summaries Fitzenia generates about your own data — for example highlighting a pattern in your logging, your calorie trend, or your weight movement. They appear as an insight card on the Dashboard and a few other surfaces, turning the numbers you already track into a quick read.

AI Insights run entirely on your device using its built-in on-device language model — Gemini Nano via Android's AI APIs, or Apple's Foundation Models on supported iPhones. Nothing about an insight is sent to a server to be generated: the model reads your local data and writes the summary on the phone, so this feature is private and works without the AI Coach subscription.

AI Insights and the AI Coach are different features. AI Insights are automatic, on-device, free narratives that appear in the app. The AI Coach is a Premium, server-side chat assistant you ask questions and that can pull in your data for a back-and-forth conversation. Don't confuse the two: a user without Premium can still see on-device AI Insights.

AI Insights are consent-gated. The first time, Fitzenia asks for your permission to generate personalized summaries from the data you already track; you can turn this on or off. Until you consent, insight cards stay off. You manage this under the app's settings alongside the other privacy controls.

On-device model availability has three states. Available means insights generate normally. Pending means the on-device model is still downloading or initializing — Gemini Nano in particular can take several minutes to download the first time — and Fitzenia shows a loading placeholder. Unavailable means the device or OS version can't run the model, so insight cards won't appear.

Because AI Insights are generated and cached locally per device, the wording you see can differ from one device to another even for the same data — that's expected. The insight cache is cleared when you sign out, and insights are regenerated as your data changes.

AI Insights are guidance and observations, not medical advice or precise prescriptions. Fitzenia deliberately keeps them to short, non-clinical summaries and filters the model's output so it doesn't make medical claims or prescribe exact gram amounts. Treat them as a helpful nudge toward your own trends, not a diagnosis.

If you don't see AI Insights: confirm you granted the insights consent in settings, give the on-device model time to finish downloading on first use (the card shows a loading state while it's Pending), and note that older or unsupported devices may not be able to run the on-device model at all. None of this affects your ability to log food or use the rest of the app.
